subject: Seedling integration: SDK compatibility and deprecation workback
messages:
From: Elena Kwon <elena@seedling.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Devin Patel <devin@toolchain.io>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Seedling - SDK compatibility with upcoming Redwood API changes

Hi Soojin,

Quick note from Seedling engineering: we ran an integration test against the v3 SDK preview and hit two breaking changes that impact our production adapter: the removal of the sync.hooks.preGenerate hook and a change in the streaming token framing that affects backpressure handling. Attached is a short impact matrix (seedling-impact-matrix.xlsx) with examples and the failing call traces.

We understand deprecations happen, but our roadmap depends on Redwood SDK behaviors for an enterprise deployment in Q1. Can you share the public schedule for the v3 cutover, and whether you can provide a compatibility shim or an LTS branch for partners on a slower upgrade cadence? Specific asks:
- A compatibility shim (or feature-flag) that restores preGenerate hook behavior or an equivalent callback.
- A target date for removal of the old streaming framing and whether an opt-in migration mode is possible.
- A contact and timeline for validation builds we can run for our customers.

Happy to hop on a quick call — I looped Devin (our integration lead) for technical details.

Thanks,
Elena Kwon
Head of Integrations, Seedling Labs
 elena@seedling.ai
Attachment: seedling-impact-matrix.xlsx (worksheet: impact-by-endpoint)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Kwon <elena@seedling.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Seedling - SDK compatibility with upcoming Redwood API changes

Elena — thanks for the details and the matrix, that really helps. I'm looping in Vanessa (partner ops) and Marcus (alliances) so we can coordinate across product & partner programs.

Short answer: we can and should work with you on a partner migration path. High level proposed next steps from my side:
1) Engineering triage on INF-2441 (we'll attach your matrix) to scope shim vs. doc work (ETA 2 business days).
2) If a small compatibility shim is feasible, we can ship a partner "compat" build as an opt-in flag for Seedling customers while we stabilize the public v3 release.
3) If shim isn't feasible, propose a 9-month deprecation window with an opt-in migration flag and clear changelog examples.
4) Schedule a partner validation call this week (30–45m) to walk through failing traces.

Can you and Devin share a short list of customer tenant IDs affected and a prioritization (P0/P1) for endpoints? I'll set up the triage and send a follow-up with owners and timelines.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Partner PM, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Kwon <elena@seedling.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Seedling - SDK compatibility with upcoming Redwood API changes

Elena — appreciate the clear matrix. A few operational notes from partner ops:

- We can create a partner-canary release track. This gives Seedling a build that re-introduces the hook behavior behind an opt-in flag so your QA can validate without impacting others.
- We'll draft a partner-facing migration playbook (examples, snippet diffs, test harness) and publish it on the partner portal.
- Proposed compatibility window: announce deprecation Jan 15, 2027; maintain opt-in compat flag and partner LTS branch through Sep 30, 2027. That gives ~9 months for integrations and customer migrations.

I'm attaching a quick patch proposal Marcus flagged for engineering to review (proposed-shim-patch.diff). Can your engineering team review the diff and confirm if it addresses the preGenerate hook semantics? Also please confirm any legal/ops constraints about exposing an opt-in behavior to your enterprise tenants.

I'll coordinate a 30-minute working session for Wed or Thu — suggested agenda: triage matrix, confirm P0 endpoints, agree on canary release date.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Program Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-shim-patch.diff

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Kwon <elena@seedling.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Seedling - SDK compatibility with upcoming Redwood API changes

Thanks everyone — summarizing the plan and owners so there's no ambiguity: 

1) INF-2441 triage (Engineering): assigned to eng-sig-sdk, initial assessment due by Tue 2026-12-07. Owner: Priya N. (SDK lead).
2) Partner canary build: if triage shows shim is small (<2 dev sprints), ship opt-in compat flag build to Seedling by 2026-12-20. Owner: eng-sig-sdk.
3) Migration playbook & test harness: Partner Ops to publish draft by 2026-12-22. Owner: Vanessa O.
4) Announce deprecation publicly: 2027-01-15 with clear timeline. Partner LTS & opt-in compat flag available until 2027-09-30.
5) Customer Validation: Seedling to provide P0 tenant IDs and run canary; schedule weekly check-ins through March. Owner: Seedling / Seedling engineering contact: Elena K.

If we find the shim would materially harm runtime performance or complicate the serving runtime (e.g., significant KV cache regressions or added latency), fallback is to prioritize the migration path and provide SDK helpers + automated refactor scripts. We need a risk sign-off from Runtime Eng for the shim.

Action items for this thread:
- Elena / Devin: send P0 endpoint list and tenant IDs by EOD Mon 2026-12-06.
- Priya (SDK) will post triage notes to INF-2441.
- Vanessa to schedule the partner validation call (Wed/Thu window).

Thanks — I'll update the Jira and link the triage notes.

Marcus Lin
VP, Alliances, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
